```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = TRUE,
  eval = requireNamespace("org.Hs.eg.db", quietly = TRUE)
)
library(rsemverse)

# A small dataset in a temporary folder, to break in different ways.
make_demo <- function() {
  dir <- tempfile("demo-")
  dir.create(file.path(dir, "data"), recursive = TRUE)
  ids <- c("ENSG00000141510.18", "ENSG00000111640.5", "ENSG00000075624.14")
  set.seed(1)
  for (s in c("A", "B")) {
    count <- round(rgamma(3, shape = 2, rate = 0.02), 1)
    tab <- data.frame(
      gene_id = ids, `transcript_id(s)` = "T", length = 1000, effective_length = 800,
      expected_count = count, TPM = round(count / sum(count) * 1e6, 2), FPKM = 0,
      check.names = FALSE
    )
    write.table(tab, file.path(dir, "data", paste0(s, ".genes.results")),
                sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
  }
  writeLines(c("sample_id,ref", "A,A.genes.results", "B,B.genes.results"),
             file.path(dir, "metadata.csv"))
  dir
}
# Runs from inside the demo folder, so that messages show the short paths
# "data" and "metadata.csv" that you would normally use.
demo_call <- function(dir, ...) {
  old <- setwd(dir)
  on.exit(setwd(old))
  rsem_read("data", "metadata.csv", species = "human", expr = "count", ...)
}
```

`rsem_read()` stops with a message whenever the input is not what it expects.
It never returns a partly filled table. The messages below are the real ones,
produced when this page was built, each from a deliberately broken dataset.

## Arguments

**`species` or `expr` is missing**

```{r}
rsem_read("data", "metadata.csv", expr = "count")
rsem_read("data", "metadata.csv", species = "human")
```

Both arguments are required. Pick `"human"` or `"mouse"`, and `"count"` or
`"tpm"`.

**The species does not match the gene IDs**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
rsem_read(file.path(d, "data"), file.path(d, "metadata.csv"),
          species = "mouse", expr = "count")
```

The IDs start with `ENSG`, so they are human. Check which genome and
annotation your RSEM reference used.

## The metadata

**A column is missing**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
writeLines(c("sample_id,file", "A,A.genes.results"), file.path(d, "metadata.csv"))
demo_call(d)
```

The columns must be named exactly `sample_id` and `ref`.

**A listed file is not in `data`**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
writeLines(c("sample_id,ref", "A,A.genes.results", "B,B_typo.genes.results"),
           file.path(d, "metadata.csv"))
demo_call(d)
```

`ref` is a path inside `data`, not a path from your working directory. For
`data = "data"` and `ref = "S1.genes.results"`, the file read is
`data/S1.genes.results`.

**Duplicated sample or file**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
writeLines(c("sample_id,ref", "A,A.genes.results", "A,B.genes.results"),
           file.path(d, "metadata.csv"))
demo_call(d)
```

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
writeLines(c("sample_id,ref", "A,A.genes.results", "B,A.genes.results"),
           file.path(d, "metadata.csv"))
demo_call(d)
```

Each sample needs its own name and its own file.

## The RSEM files

**A column is missing from one file**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
f <- file.path(d, "data", "B.genes.results")
tab <- read.delim(f, check.names = FALSE, colClasses = c(gene_id = "character"))
tab$expected_count <- NULL
write.table(tab, f, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
demo_call(d)
```

The file does not look like RSEM gene-level output, or it is a transcript-level
(`isoforms.results`) file. Use the `*.genes.results` files.

**The files contain different genes, or the same genes in another order**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
f <- file.path(d, "data", "B.genes.results")
tab <- read.delim(f, check.names = FALSE, colClasses = c(gene_id = "character"))
write.table(tab[c(2, 1, 3), ], f, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
demo_call(d)
```

All samples must come from the same RSEM reference. If you edited or sorted a
file by hand, run RSEM again or restore the original.

**A value is not a number, or is missing**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
f <- file.path(d, "data", "A.genes.results")
tab <- read.delim(f, check.names = FALSE, colClasses = c(gene_id = "character"))
tab$expected_count[2] <- NA
write.table(tab, f, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
demo_call(d)
```

**A gene appears twice in one file**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
f <- file.path(d, "data", "A.genes.results")
tab <- read.delim(f, check.names = FALSE, colClasses = c(gene_id = "character"))
tab$gene_id[2] <- tab$gene_id[1]
write.table(tab, f, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
demo_call(d)
```

## The annotation

**The OrgDb package is not installed**

If `org.Hs.eg.db` (human) or `org.Mm.eg.db` (mouse) is missing, the message
is:

```text
The package 'org.Mm.eg.db' is required. Install it with BiocManager::install("org.Mm.eg.db").
```

Install the package for the species you use. The two packages are not
installed together with rsemverse, so you only need the one you use.

**The gene IDs are not Ensembl IDs**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
for (s in c("A", "B")) {
  f <- file.path(d, "data", paste0(s, ".genes.results"))
  tab <- read.delim(f, check.names = FALSE, colClasses = c(gene_id = "character"))
  tab$gene_id <- c("TP53", "GAPDH", "ACTB")
  write.table(tab, f, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
}
demo_call(d)
```

The files are already named by symbol, so there is nothing to look up.
`rsem_read()` needs Ensembl IDs (with or without a version).

**A gene ID equals a gene symbol**

```{r}
d <- make_demo()
for (s in c("A", "B")) {
  f <- file.path(d, "data", paste0(s, ".genes.results"))
  tab <- read.delim(f, check.names = FALSE, colClasses = c(gene_id = "character"))
  tab$gene_id <- c("ENSG00000141510.18", "TP53", "ENSG00000075624.14")
  write.table(tab, f, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
}
demo_call(d)
```

An ID without a symbol is kept under its own name, so it cannot share a name
with a symbol. Rename or remove that gene in your files.

## Things that are not errors

**Many genes are kept under their Ensembl ID.** These are genes without a
symbol in the OrgDb. In the [real-data
check](https://daikikumakura.github.io/rsemverse/articles/real-data.html),
about 39% of the genes were in this group, but they held only a few percent of
the counts. See [How it works](how-it-works.html), section 6.

**A different symbol than expected.** Symbols come from the installed OrgDb
version, which is printed in the message. Different versions can use different
symbols for the same gene.

**Counts are not integers.** RSEM reports expected counts. They are returned
unchanged; round them yourself if a tool needs integers.
